subject: Lionel Messi
title: Messi's penalty slump and Miami's HR problem

lines.vo: Lionel Messi has missed three penalties in a row.
lines.footage: Messi penalty run-up, Nashville match (check for burned-in captions)

lines.vo: Two at the World Cup. One at Nashville in August. The first run like that since 2014.

lines.vo: Inter Miami have had three head coaches this year. Messi is the only constant.

lines.vo: Coaches arrive. Coaches leave. Messi gives the induction. He is the club's HR department.
He finished fifth in the Ballon d'Or and skipped the gala. Fifth. Most players would frame it.

facts_used: Three penalty misses in a row: two at the World Cup (Austria, Egypt), then Nashville on 15 Aug; first such run since 2014 (research pack roast_now; the Nashville clip is an unverified viral_moments search link)
Inter Miami have had three head coaches in 2026: Mascherano, Hoyos (interim), Kily Gonzalez from 15 Sep; Messi the constant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Inter_Miami_CF_season)
Messi finished fifth in the 2026 Ballon d'Or, skipped the gala and stayed in Miami for the Messi Cup, a U-16 tournament (https://www.si.com/soccer/lionel-messi-2026-ballon-dor-ranking-revealed)
Eight Ballon d'Or awards, a record (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi)
Miami led Charlotte 3-0 after 42 minutes, drew 3-3; Messi not among the scorers (https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/20232/inter-miami-cf)
notes: The penalty miss streak is a stat tease only and is not linked to his father's death (no-joke rule). The Nashville penalty clip is unverified, so confirm the footage before airing. Insert gags are fiction with generic characters and a caricature of Messi, with no factual claims. after_line counts from 1. Current hair and beard look unverified. Punch-up pass: HR-department running gag is called back at the end (line 8). 'Bad run, great career' is a mild roast and praise pair; no joke links the penalty misses to anything personal.
